steps.say: Drug-induced lupus copies idiopathic disease without its kidneys and brain. Procainamide and hydralazine are the top of the risk list. Symptoms start months after exposure and fade after withdrawal. Every new lupus picture requires a full drug history.
steps.tx: Drug-induced lupus erythematosus (**DILE**, medication triggered autoimmunity) is an idiosyncratic reaction starting months to years after continuous exposure, fading after prompt withdrawal. Definite high-risk drugs are **procainamide** (up to **20 percent** incidence, the highest) and **hydralazine** (**5 to 8 percent**), with moderate risk from minocycline, diltiazem, quinidine, and penicillamine. New lupus features on these drugs indicate DILE first, because stopping early prevents organ injury.

vis.alt: Drug hapten binding with mast cell degranulation and maculopapular cutaneous drug rash.
vis.caption: Drugs turn immunogenic as haptens and trigger lupus-like autoimmunity. Exposure history dates the disease. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Slow acetylators are the accumulators of toxic metabolites of procainamide and hydralazine. NAT2 status is the decider of the risk. The same drugs are cleared safely by fast acetylators. Genotype explains why only some exposed patients fall ill.
steps.tx: Slow hepatic N-acetyltransferase 2 (**NAT2**, a drug clearing liver enzyme) acetylators carry marked susceptibility to procainamide and hydralazine lupus. Delayed clearance accumulates reactive toxic **hydroxylamine** metabolites that drive autoimmunity. Slow acetylation with prolonged exposure indicates the highest risk group, while fast acetylators clear the same doses safely.

steps.say: Anti-histone antibodies are the markers of classic DILE in above 95 to 100 percent. They target the H2A-H2B dimer. Half of idiopathic SLE carries them too, so they never prove idiopathic disease. Anti-dsDNA and anti-Sm instead are the proof of idiopathic lupus.
steps.tx: Classic systemic DILE carries anti-**histone** antibodies (against DNA spool proteins) in above **95 to 100 percent**, locked onto the **H2A-H2B** dimer in procainamide and hydralazine cases. The same antibodies appear in **50 percent** of idiopathic SLE, so alone they prove nothing. Anti-**dsDNA**, anti-**Sm**, and deep hypocomplementemia stay absent in classic DILE, while anti TNF inhibitor disease breaks the rule with full idiopathic serology.

steps.say: Systemic DILE gives fever, fatigue, weight loss with symmetric joint pains and serositis. Kidneys and brain are characteristically spared. Pleurisy and pericarditis are the dominant serositis pair. Renal or CNS disease points away from classic DILE.
steps.tx: Fever with fatigue, weight loss, symmetric **polyarthralgias** (aching in many joints), and **serositis** (inflamed pleura or pericardium) form the systemic DILE syndrome. Kidneys and brain stay characteristically untouched, and that sparing is the bedside split from idiopathic lupus. Lupus features without renal or CNS hits on a culprit drug indicate DILE.

steps.say: Drug-induced SCLE gives widespread annular sun-exposed lesions with anti-Ro positivity. Terbinafine, thiazides, calcium blockers, PPIs, and checkpoint inhibitors are the triggers. Lesions fade after withdrawal. Sunscreen alone is never sufficient while the drug continues.
steps.tx: Sunlight brings out **DI-SCLE** (drug-induced subacute cutaneous lupus, medication triggered photosensitive rash) as widespread annular or papulosquamous plaques with anti-**Ro SSA** positivity. **Terbinafine**, thiazide diuretics, calcium channel blockers, proton pump inhibitors, and checkpoint inhibitors head the trigger list. Ring shaped sun-exposed plaques starting after a new prescription indicate DI-SCLE, fading over weeks once withdrawn.

vis.alt: Photosensitive annular plaques with vacuolar interface dermatitis on skin biopsy in SCLE.
vis.caption: Annular sun-exposed plaques with interface dermatitis define SCLE. Drug triggers fade after withdrawal. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Cure is permanent stoppage of the trigger with steroids as a bridge. Symptoms are cleared over weeks to months. Rechallenge is never attempted. A structurally unrelated replacement is required for the original indication.
steps.tx: Cure is immediate permanent cessation of the trigger drug, with symptoms clearing over weeks to months. Temporary low dose oral **glucocorticoids** bridge active serositis or arthritis during clearance. Rechallenge reproduces disease within days and is never attempted. The original indication requires a structurally unrelated replacement with documented tolerance.

steps.say: Minocycline lupus is the disease of young women on acne therapy with joint pains and liver features. Low platelets are added by quinidine to the picture. Both resolve after withdrawal. Acne and arrhythmia each require a new agent.
steps.tx: Young women on long acne courses develop **minocycline** lupus with joint pains, autoimmune liver inflammation, and ANCA positivity. **Quinidine** paints thrombocytopenia across the same lupus canvas. Both pictures wash out over weeks after withdrawal. Fresh acne or rhythm therapy comes from an unrelated class, because same-class switches re-trigger disease.

steps.say: Every lupus presentation is interrogated for procainamide, hydralazine, minocycline, and newer triggers. Anti-histone positivity without renal disease supports DILE. Withdrawal is both the test and the cure. Idiopathic therapy is reserved for true idiopathic disease.
steps.tx: Every lupus presentation requires interrogation for **procainamide** up to **20 percent**, **hydralazine 5 to 8 percent**, minocycline, diltiazem, quinidine, penicillamine, terbinafine, thiazides, PPIs, and checkpoint inhibitors. Anti-**histone** above **95 percent** without renal or CNS disease supports DILE, while anti-**dsDNA** proves idiopathic disease. Withdrawal is the test and the cure together.
